headline: This law extends the Paycheck Protection Program for small businesses through June 30, 2021, with limits on new applications during the final month.
what_it_does: The Paycheck Protection Program, created to help small businesses during the COVID-19 pandemic, was set to end on March 31, 2021. This law pushes the end date to June 30, 2021. During the final 30 days, from June 1 to June 30, the Small Business Administration may only process applications submitted before June 1 and may not accept new loan applications. The law also keeps its budget effects out of certain federal spending-scorecard rules.

who_it_affects.group: Small businesses seeking pandemic relief loans
who_it_affects.how: They can apply for Paycheck Protection Program loans until the program closes, but applications submitted on or after June 1, 2021 will not be accepted.
They must keep processing already-submitted applications through June 30 but cannot take in new loan applications during June.

who_it_affects.group: Lenders participating in the Paycheck Protection Program
who_it_affects.how: They can continue making program loans through June 30, with the June 1 cutoff for new applications applying to them as well.

when_it_takes_effect: Upon enactment on March 30, 2021; the extended program runs through June 30, 2021.
